label: Resilient Well-Connected Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal depression on the PHQ-9, and virtually negligible anxiety on the GAD-7. The pattern suggests a stable, socially connected individual with strong emotional resilience.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness, indicating strong and satisfying social connections
Exhibits near-floor depressive symptom scores, suggesting stable positive mood
Displays virtually no anxiety symptoms, reflecting effective stress management or low perceived stress
Maintains moderate screen or social media use (1–3 hours), suggesting balanced digital engagement
Higher educational attainment may contribute to access to coping resources and social capital

label: High-Distress Heavy-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on social media and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.67), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.16) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. With 179 respondents in this cluster, the profile represents a sizable subgroup characterized by compounded mental health challenges alongside heavy digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Heavy social media use exceeding 5 hours per day
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean 2.16)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety symptoms

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.23, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.80, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating generally robust mental well-being.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, spending 1–3 hours of daily screen/online time
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology, well below clinical concern
Demonstrates low anxiety levels consistent with healthy psychological functioning
Maintains moderate daily screen or online usage (1–3 hours), suggesting balanced digital engagement
Higher educational attainment may contribute to stronger coping resources and social connectedness
